subject: Panel closeout: Amaya Singh — reconcile anchors & lock scores
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Panel closeout: Amaya Singh — reconcile anchors & lock scores

Morning all — quick closeout on Amaya (Data Engineer). I pulled everyone's scorecards and there are a couple of notable gaps on System Design and Ownership that we should reconcile before I change candidate status in Greenhouse. Attached: Amaya_Singh_scorecard.pdf (compiled), Amaya_Singh_resume.pdf.

High-level ask: can folks lock final anchored scores by 12:00 PM PT today? If there's a remaining disagreement >1 point on a rubric axis we'll assign a tiebreak owner (see below).

Quick context:
- Interview loop: Eng + Systems design + Product.
- Current provisional scores (avg): Technical 4.0, Design 3.2, Ownership 3.0.

Proposal for how to reconcile:
1) Each interviewer: add 1–2 bullet justification to the scorecard and reply here.
2) If variance >1 for any axis, Lauren to own tiebreak.
3) If we land on a borderline hire (3.0–3.4 avg), we discuss a focused reference check and a short follow-up exercise.

Action items:
- Marissa: share 1–2 bullets on why you gave Design a 3
- Karthik: share examples you leaned on for the 4 on Technical
- Lauren: be prepared to run tiebreak if needed

I'll lock status after replies and ping the recruiter to hold any offer communication until we're aligned.

Thanks — V.

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Hiring Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Amaya_Singh_scorecard.pdf (compiled interviewer notes + raw scores)
- Amaya_Singh_resume.pdf

On Wed, Nov 3, 2026 at 9:05 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Morning all — quick closeout on Amaya (Data Engineer)...

Thanks, Vanessa — quick note from my side. I scored Design a 3 because: 
- The decomposition was good but Amaya didn't surface tradeoffs for sharded state under heavy tail latency (important for our infra).
- Their API contract sketch was serviceable but lacked explicit metrics/SLIs to guard gradual rollout.

I added a short justification to the attached compiled scorecard (page 2). If Karthik can point to a concrete example where she explicitly handled those concerns, I'm willing to move to a 3.5 -> but I'm comfortable with 3 as final.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Staff Engineer, Compute
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Panel closeout: Amaya Singh — reconcile anchors & lock scores

Vanessa / team — I pushed a couple of comments into karthik_notes.txt and added inline notes to the scorecard (attached). TL;DR on why I scored Technical a 4:
- She quickly identified the bottleneck as KV-cache invalidation during writes and sketched an incremental migration path (shadow rollout + feature flag + data-versioning) which matches what we've done before.
- She described a concrete test plan for the migration (canary traffic, steady-state metrics), including what to measure and rollback thresholds.

On Design: Marissa, I think Amaya implied an approach to handle tail latency by prioritizing causal reads and async reconciliation — I agree it's not spelled out but the intent was there. I'm flexible to average the two positions (3 and 4) and use a weighted average favoring technical depth for this role (i.e., technical axis weight 1.2).

If we follow Vanessa's process and Lauren runs the tiebreak, I'm fine deferring.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Manager, Inference Systems
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- karthik_notes.txt (short bulleted evidence)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-03T17:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Panel closeout: Amaya Singh — reconcile anchors & lock scores

Thanks for the notes. I compiled a reconciliation table in the scorecard and landed final anchored numbers by axis after weighing technical depth slightly higher (as Karthik suggested):
- Technical: 4 (avg -> 4.0 after weight)
- System Design: 3 (final)
- Ownership: 3 (final)

Final composite: 3.4 (borderline). Given the borderline result I recommend:
1) Lauren to run a targeted reference check focusing on system ownership and execution history (I'll take this).
2) If references align, extend offer with an immediate 3-month success plan (measurable milestones).
3) If references are mixed, we pass.

I updated Greenhouse with provisional "Hold - pending references" and left a short note summarizing the anchor decisions. Vanessa — if you're comfortable I will call the recruiter to pause outreach and run the refs tomorrow morning.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Engineering
Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. Lauren, please own the reference check and update this thread with notes (and add any red flags you see). Marissa / Karthik — appreciate the clarifying bullets; no further action from your side unless Lauren asks for specific follow-ups.

Recruiter: please hold offer and any candidate-facing communication until Lauren posts reference outcome here. If refs are positive we'll proceed with a short-form offer outlining the 3-month success plan; if not, we'll close out.

I'll mark the GH status to "On hold — references" and will not progress any offers without explicit confirmation here.
